title: Pause + Return
concept: Turns “I need space” into a promise rather than a slammed door: time apart, with a set time to come back. Asking for a pause is never penalised. It’s one of the tools we lean on most.
whenToUse: When either of you is flooded — racing heart, tunnel vision, can’t think straight, an urge to flee or win. Any time it’s not calm enough to have an honest conversation.
steps: Say it — “I need a pause.” No explanation needed.
Set a time — pick a return time (20 minutes minimum, 24 hours max): “I’ll be ready at ___.”
Step away — get calm (walk, shower, breathe, music). Don’t rehearse the argument in your head.
Come back — reconnect at the time you said, even briefly, to prove it’s a pause, not a disappearance.
Restart warm — warm up and check it’s safe, before going back to “where you left off.”

phrases.text: I’m not leaving you; I just need to get calm.

working: B: “I’m flooded. I need a pause. I’ll be ready at 8.30pm.” A: “Okay. Thank you for giving a time. I’ll see you at 8.30pm.” They return at 8.30pm, even for two minutes, then restart warm.
notWorking: “I need space.” (walks away) “We’ll talk later.” — “Later” isn’t a return time, and it can feel like being abandoned. Fix: always give an exact time.
activity: Agree your default length (say, 20 minutes) and your max (24 hours). Agree your phrases out loud and write them down. Practise once this week on something minor, and keep the return time.
warn: For flooding, never for fear. If threats, fear, coercion or violence appear, do not return at the set time: leave safely and use the Help Lines.
